related_questions.question: How many people have left California since COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: Since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, California has experienced a net loss of residents, with more people leaving the state than moving in. Between 2022 and 2023, over 690,000 people left California for other states. However, the state also saw an influx of new residents, with just over 422,000 people moving into California from other parts of the US during the same period. This resulted in a net loss of around 268,000 residents.
snippet_highlighted_words: Between 2022 and 2023, over 690,000 people left California for other states

text_blocks.snippet: Several factors have contributed to this trend, including the high cost of living in California, particularly housing costs. Many Californians have sought more affordable living options in other states.

list.title: Net Out-Migration:
list.snippet: California has seen a significant net loss of residents, with more people leaving the state than moving in.

list.title: Reasons for Leaving:
list.snippet: Cost of living, particularly housing costs, is a major driver. Other factors include lifestyle preferences and the desire for a different environment.

list.title: Destinations:
list.snippet: Texas, Arizona, Nevada, and Florida are among the states that have seen a significant influx of Californians.

list.title: Rebounding Population:
list.snippet: While there was a significant population decline initially, data from the US Census Bureau suggests the state's population has shown signs of rebounding and is approaching pre-pandemic levels.
